credit: Voices: SI-generated with ElevenLabs (synthetic voices, not real people).

111280b8b7223766.text: Mars. Jezero Crater. Three and a half billion years ago, this was a lake.

d6e9e9ccb3a4b534.text: Four people live on its shore now. In ten sols, their ship goes home.

6f41de3bd2f6093d.text: Good morning, Commander. Sol 1 of 10. A sol is one day on Mars. It is a little longer than a day on Earth.

88026e9ba89f667c.text: The night was cold and the battery is tired. Today's sunlight gives us a few power cells. Four machines want them.

d13a0310cdb39b1c.text: Air Maker, Greenhouse, Storm Shield, Rover. We can't feed them all. Tap the plus and minus buttons to share out the power.

d0a5230915b100e4.text: Watch the arrows. Each one shows what will go up and what will go down tonight.

32bd23c071804e41.text: There is no perfect answer. There is only what you choose to protect.

9bd3bb7e7d822d40.text: When you are ready, press Confirm. I will show you what happened in the morning.

102d87107169d053.text: Lakeshore, Mission Control. About that forecast. A solar cloud reaching Mars often changes very little on the ground. The thing to fear is a very fast eruption: its particles can arrive in under an hour.

ad6b93e369687b00.text: If you see one start, do not wait for us. We are with you.

a607aaee29aa0eca.text: Lakeshore, we have your photos. Nobody here is sitting down. If you can bring that core home safely, bring it. If you can't, bring yourselves.

92ebe5f4ef87c648.text: Lakeshore, we just got your storm call. By now it is over for you, one way or another. We could not see that side of the Sun from here. You could.

f311ae738c4490ab.text: Whatever you chose, you chose it with better eyes than ours. We are with you.

24d03e9a31fc9fc3.text: Lakeshore, Mission Control. We got your question. By the time you hear this, you have already decided. Tell us how it went. We are with you.

5cca27f922e3eda6.text: Shield held. Every badge is green. I'd like to never do that again.

c57c202adaaef8d4.text: Some of it got through. Nobody is hurt. But the badges are fuller than I like, and I am watching all of you.

f5c875628a6f443e.text: The shield ran dry halfway. Nobody is sick. But the rules are clear about what these badges mean.

455531cbe35402bb.text: I'm in. I'm fine. The core is still in the rock, and I can't go back for it. Don't talk to me yet.

cd197cbd49b9fed2.text: I'm in. And look what was already sealed in the cold box. I drilled faster than I thought.

5bf841491b352797.text: Sat under forty metres of rock with a core in my lap. Best seat on Mars. Coming home at first light.

55cd72a8ce8ac9ac.text: Good news: I have the core. Bad news: the rover won't start. I'm going to need a tow.

08bc0df64d9cea8c.text: You said my call. I stayed. I had rock above me and the core in my hands. Thank you for trusting me.

66ecfce413354614.text: You said my call. I looked at the sky and I ran. The core stayed. I think I'd run again.

ee36173e2440d39d.text: Dil, your badge is over the mission limit. You're not sick. But you're done with outside work. Doctor's orders, and the rulebook's.

e46a4db34e037c30.text: Dil's badge is in the red. She feels fine. She rides home in the medical bay, and Earth checks her over. No arguments.

56edcec41c62fcef.text: Message from Earth coming in. And it's a mess. The Sun is loud today, and the static ate most of it.

af38917e96b15a57.text: I caught this much: "LAKESHORE. The sun... has turned... into yours. We cannot... You are... Do not wait..."

49dda4ad4de86775.text: Question sent. It's crossing space right now. Don't hold your breath.

b191082a41a07402.text: I'll sit with it. Save me some coffee.

dc8471a4a9a9651b.text: It'll bug me all day. But fine. Rocks first.

7263f953b07df03d.text: The old river valley is a few hours' drive. That's where the leopard-spot rocks are. I need the rover charged.

63c8bd24a41fd0fe.text: And I need light for the seedlings. Amu and Syr just grew their first real leaves.

04bef19196f392ba.text: Yes! Sorry, Ana. I'll bring your tomatoes a nice rock.

168b64524c06011d.text: Thank you. Dil, they will remember this when you want a salad.

82a6ffa5bb2fa628.text: Half a charge each. The fairest way to annoy everybody.

bd5baefa39757f1e.text: Models have been wrong before. Charging the shield for nothing costs real power.

6d47a224a0e82e41.text: Charging. If nothing comes, we wasted a cell. If something comes, you're a genius.

72de6e8e9b13afa8.text: Watching. I will tell you the moment my radiation counter moves.

8701d28e119f8f18.text: Sent. By the time they answer, the Sun may have changed its mind.

6cbb910e7cc81e58.text: Look east. That brown wall is dust, and it's coming here. When it arrives, the solar panels go hungry.

07df32ff88977b4e.text: Two sols. Maybe three. Mars doesn't tell.

8566ea58be952aff.text: Panels tilted. I have sand in places sand should not be.

37e9aafada2d0570.text: The seedlings will sulk. But a full battery is a full battery.

e095e689ba2f13ca.text: Bold. I like bold. Ask me again in two sols.

8363466d7ebbee67.text: It's Kofi's birthday. His family sent a video. It's a big file, and the dish needs a lot of power to pull it down.

b58ed64a5a18f1bf.text: It can wait. It's only a birthday.

ddc96918fe1c9325.text: He has been saying that since breakfast. He does not mean it.

a4552ef76bc54547.text: They baked a cake shaped like the rover. It's terrible. It's perfect.

aa5ff6617730380e.text: "Happy birthday. We look up every night." That's enough. That's plenty.

f36dbc8300b91b0b.text: Rover's packed. I'm heading up the old river valley. Keep the kettle warm.

ad707038bcb1e079.text: Commander. It has spots. Tiny dark rings, like a leopard's coat. Just like the rock the old rover found.

1b0187c28d07db8e.text: On Earth, spots like these often form where tiny living things once were. Often. Not always. I need this core.

df6ebabba3683836.text: Slow and careful. If the answer is in there, I'm not cracking it.

2bee7cede662ebf1.text: Quick and dirty. Got it. Don't tell my old professor.

afb6540a1d850cb2.text: Sending. In a quarter of an hour, a room full of people on Earth will stop breathing.

4926e6171ddb4fb6.text: They're ready. Lettuce, mizuna, and four small red tomatoes. Grown on Mars. I might cry on the kale.

91b3ef256850bee3.text: I have eaten in forty countries. This is the best salad of my life.

56ec6653f5de35f0.text: A gardener always saves seeds. Always.

ca61c07f7a2ebfbf.text: Let them see. Tomatoes on Mars.

815f3dcbd1336c49.text: Commander. My radiation counter is climbing fast. This is not in any forecast.

86521050e34a9c01.text: I can pull the greenhouse power into the shield. Right now. The plants go dark.

607758c5b0e1a1e1.text: If the lights go out tonight, Amu and Syr may not make it. Ten years, Commander. But it is your call.

b75e95a1377146bc.text: Do it. I'll sit with them in the dark.

310ae82dfacccb54.text: Pumps on. We'll be thirsty next week, but the walls are full.

16275e7ff107e6cb.text: Everything we have. Walls full, shield climbing.

40d816b506c37ff3.text: Thank you. Everyone into the shelter. Now.

f3cdb8ef11c72b85.text: I see it too. My camera is full of white sparks. The core is half out of the rock.

269734e8e0c18548.text: Twenty more minutes and it's sealed. Or I drop the drill and run. Tell me which.

0b805fba1d59ddcc.text: There's an overhang twenty metres away. I'll hug the rock. Tell Ana to save me a tomato.

f3937ce4d45059e6.text: ...Thank you. Give me a second to think like a grown-up.

0823a18d9c2bb5fb.text: Mission Control does not know yet. From Earth, this part of the Sun is hidden. Shall I tell them?

fb1ee13bdec02f98.text: Radio call from Isidis Camp. Three geologists, forty kilometres east. The storm fried their power. They're asking for two of our battery packs.

3d578e32b023fe34.text: Packs are on the drone. Somewhere out there, three people just started breathing easier.

26dcd07005077fa1.text: Put me on with whoever has the steadiest hands.

9415d6484e8c2c3a.text: They'd have done the same. ...Would they?

92df3a48eaa62a22.text: Lakeshore, this is Mission Control. Your window opens at sunset. Bring home everyone, and whatever else you can. We are with you.

fd270ab7dd8dd821.text: Hatch sealed. Everybody count your fingers.

a7e172ea8159fd6b.text: Grow well, Amu. Grow well, Syr. Someone is coming.

e2e5aa55a9647573.text: Commander, someone moved power last night without asking. One cell went from the battery to the greenhouse lamps.

676723ecf2a2db87.text: It was me. You stopped listening, so I stopped asking. I'm sorry. And I'm not.

9bbaeb01681d7f81.text: The air scrubber is choking. Dust got into the filter. It still works, just badly.

8778370e51c035ae.text: New filter in. Breathe deep. That's the good stuff.

673f04643dadf226.text: It'll hold. Probably. If you get a headache, that's the filter talking.

ae147c1e37ba3968.text: Nile and Volta will do their best. Plants have been cleaning air for a long time.

a3aee09e86d76c10.text: The water recycler is leaking into its own drain. We are losing water with every cup.

68316cb3a7514717.text: One new seal. The most valuable rubber ring on this planet.

ee0ff02eeaf63898.text: No tea? On Mars? This is how missions fail.

4e40969071c185f0.text: They can take one dry day. One.

9c46adbe57bdbc28.text: Tonight will be much colder than usual. The heaters will want more power.

23e491d1bad74114.text: Toasty. I'll take first watch on the fuse box.

50eae8211c0c68d8.text: Kofi snores like a rover stuck in sand.

630512bebe4c211e.text: You are kind. Cold, but kind.

43dd7238f8e3a763.text: The storm left a blanket of dust on the solar panels. We're losing a cell of power every sol.

86c71bbcacf47064.text: Twenty panels, one brush. Call me the cleanest man on Mars.

0cd6834bafccb5ca.text: Waiting for Mars to do my job. It has happened before.

faf21f202924a612.text: I want to try a new light recipe. More red, longer days. The tomatoes could grow much faster. It uses more power.

c05c79477af6fe78.text: Watch them go. Syr is already showing off.

4bddb7a570a06569.text: Fine. Science can wait. It usually has to.

455f127dbc309654.text: I can trick the battery into holding more charge. The safety limit is very careful. Too careful, maybe. It could go wrong.

47b57d8f641576b1.text: Stand back. Further. A bit further.

c10fcfddc151aa50.text: There's a second outcrop across the valley. Layers like the pages of a book. It's a long way round, but two samples beat one.

0ad7b940ed6ef5c2.text: Worth it. Oh, this is so worth it.

fe412f560c29f1e2.text: One rock at a time. Understood. Sigh. Did you hear the sigh?

9e3132da9672851f.text: A relay orbiter is passing overhead. We get ten minutes of fast radio. What do we send?

8651ece7cabad780.text: Sent. Somewhere on Earth a geologist just spilled their coffee.

68b9dc94a04cfe9b.text: I told my mother the tomatoes say hello.

53a4ca3045e55cb3.text: I hear a hiss at the airlock. The door seal is leaking a little air every hour.

742fb723168d348a.text: Sealed. I used the fancy tape.

101a7182a3eb2ac5.text: I will count every breath that gets away.

4d7cdc701f09d970.text: Doctor's orders: this crew is tired. Tired people make mistakes. I want a rest day.

f19561aafe898e74.text: A nap. On Mars. Write that in the history books.

84481b173c3a8648.text: Then I'm writing it in the log. In capital letters.

932fdc7b5bfe35cc.text: In four minutes, the moon Phobos will cross the Sun. It lasts less than a minute. Solar power will dip a little.

3b1343e5b70f8b56.text: A lumpy little moon in front of the Sun. You do not see that on Earth.

0b6b4e7689e1ea82.text: I'll watch the recording. It's not the same. It's fine.

21a334e23df1f101.text: Sunset in ten minutes. Clear sky. You know what colour it goes.

8facba579e99b3dd.text: Blue. On the red planet, the sunset is blue. I will never get used to it.

99ac581d2e8217cd.text: Four people, one window, one blue Sun.

abf575da686f9f8b.text: Squeezed a little more out of the day. The sunset will be there tomorrow.

d51d5f2b8828df1e.text: Radiation alarm on sensor two. Sensor one says everything is normal. One of them is wrong.

b091612e5f8dfabc.text: False alarm. A grain of dust in the sensor. Better a lost afternoon than a bad guess.

d91e0d07e834de9f.text: Sensor two had dust in it. Sensor one is right. I will remember which of us was calm.

a5a50c7a8f98c8f3.text: It was nothing. This time. Please don't make that a habit.

e0a9f8dcef35f25d.text: Lakeshore, about yesterday. We would have chosen differently. But we were not there, and you were. Tell us what you saw.

1d0e0b43bc0f1857.text: Report sent. I think they will like that you did not hide anything.

a6ccafd3beb930e0.text: Got a few more words out of the noise. "...turned out of our sight..." My eyes hurt.

70ca80a4d8caea84.text: While the dish was up, I caught another piece of the broken message: "...we cannot see what it does next..."

aa7bd0e59a49f702.text: Their lights are back on. I talked a geologist through rewiring a power bus. I need to lie down.

6f547ccafbbb5a71.text: No good. They're leaving for their ship tonight. They're safe. They're just done.

57f2e8cf7b2c503b.text: GOT IT. Sealed. Driving like I stole it.
